title: What happens if you take an ice bath every day?

lines.text: What happens if you take an ice bath every single day?
Day one. You gasp uncontrollably. That gasp drowns more people than the cold does.
Day five. The gasp is half as strong. Your body is learning.
Month one. Each dip spikes your noradrenaline fivefold. You feel unstoppable.
After the gym? It blunts your muscle growth.
Then you fall through ice. You don't panic. You float until the gasp passes.
You survived. Comment what stupid shenanigans Gary should try tomorrow.

experiment.payoff: useful takeaway: 1-10-1 rule for falling through ice
experiment.length: ~30 s (80 words; old scripts ran ~2.6 words/s)
facts: Cold shock (gasp + hyperventilation) causes many cold-water drownings in the first minutes, before hypothermia: Tipton, 'Cold water immersion: sudden death and prolonged survival', The Lancet 2003
Repeated immersions (~5) roughly halve the cold shock response: Tipton et al., habituation studies (Exp Physiol / J Physiol)
Immersion in 14 C water raised plasma noradrenaline ~5x: Sramek et al., Eur J Appl Physiol 2000
Cold water immersion after strength training attenuated muscle gains: Roberts et al., J Physiol 2015
1-10-1 rule (1 min cold shock, 10 min useful movement, 1 h to hypothermia): Giesbrecht, Cold Water Boot Camp
